title: Seasonal warmth had no clear ozone interaction in US bird richness records in 1995-2024
abstract: We tested whether warmer seasons changed the ozone association with recorded bird species richness. We used a published US Breeding Bird Survey panel with EPA ozone and NOAA climate data. We added survey temperature from the shared BBS source. Four models covered East and West and 1995-2009 and 2010-2024. They controlled for route-observer pairs, region-year changes, climate, and survey conditions. Interaction estimates ranged from -0.29 to +0.28 species per 10 ppb ozone per 2 C warmth anomaly. All 95% intervals included zero. All four-test corrected intervals also included zero. The pooled estimate was -0.03 species, with a 95% interval of -0.39 to +0.34. The planned test did not show a common stronger negative ozone slope in warm seasons. The test measures seasonal weather associations, not heat waves or a causal climate effect. Observation error, exposure error, monitor selection, and few western state clusters limit inference. The package preserves code, input evidence, source hashes, numerical checks, and reproduction instructions.

display.caption: Warmth-ozone interaction estimates in four US region-period samples. Dark lines show 95% intervals. Light lines show intervals with correction for four tests. All intervals include zero.

citations.reason: We use its signed derived panel, source records, and raw-data retrieval code. We test an interaction that its average-effect models did not test.
